text: Exactness for the infinite $G$. $A_n^+/J_n\cong\mathbb Z^{r}\oplus T$, $T$ a finite 2-group with invariants $2^{v_i}$, so index_logp at modulus $2^E$ is $\sum_i\min(v_i,E)+Er$. The rank $r$ is known exactly: by Quillen's theorem $\mathrm{gr}\,\mathbb Q[G]\cong U(\mathrm{gr}\,G\otimes\mathbb Q)$, so $r_n$ is the sum of the coefficients at $t^1..t^{n-1}$ of $\prod_i(1-t^i)^{-h_i}$ with the torsion-free ranks $h=(2,1,2,0)$: $r_n=2,6,14,27,47,78$ for $n=2..7$; for $n\le6$ it equals the number of columns without a pivot in B. If $\mathrm{index}(E_2)-\mathrm{index}(E_1)=r(E_2-E_1)$, then every $v_i\le E_1$, and for an element of finite order (its image is torsion) membership modulo $2^{E_2}$, $E_2>E_1$, is exact. section: 6.5. A GPU kernel for the dense Howell form modulo $2^{32}$ (prototype)

text: Algorithm. The Howell form of §2, blocked by panels of $b=256$ columns. On a panel, only the rows that are nonzero there take part; the column steps run as in c/hw.h (pivot of least 2-adic valuation, normalised to $2^v$, exact division, the row $2^{E-v}\cdot$pivot into the pool), and every step is recorded as coefficients $G$ on the pivot rows. Then the pivot rows on the trailing columns are $(I-SG_{\rm piv})^{-1}SO$ (a unit lower triangular inverse by doubling), and every other row gets $O+G\cdot P$: one product (rows $\times b$)$\cdot$($b\times$ rest), the bulk of the work.
section: 6.5. A GPU kernel for the dense Howell form modulo $2^{32}$ (prototype)

text: The product modulo $2^{32}$, exactly. Three backends, each checked at start against an exact integer product: u32 (integer matmul with wrap-around), f32 (bytes in float32: for the shift $s$, $\sum_{i+j=s}a_ib_j$ over 64-column chunks is $<2^{24}$, exact; 10 byte products, $i+j\le3$) and i8 (signed bytes on INT8 tensor cores through torch._int_mm; the int32 accumulator never wraps). The last is the scheme of the Ozaki-II analogy; on the CPU only the first two run.

text: Relator rows. Words builds $\mu(r)-1$ by shifts: $v\cdot\mu(x_g^e)=\sum_kC(e,k)\,v\,a_g^k$, and $v\cdot a_g$ moves the block of degree $k$ to degree $k+1$, one indexed write; products of powers of words still go through Alg.mul. text: Memory. The form is kept by blocks (the rows of a panel only from its first column on: half of the dense $k\times M$, 5.8 GiB at $n=7$). howell() takes the rows as pieces $(c_0,R)$ in increasing $c_0$ and puts a piece into the pool only at the panel containing $c_0$; before that its rows take part in no step, so the result is the same (checked: pieces against the whole matrix, the canonical forms coincide). The closure feeds the previous form block by block and frees each block as it goes; the shifts are taken only of the rows that are nonzero below the top degree (about 9 300 rows at $n=7$, 2.1 GB per shift matrix). The peak of the closure (two shift matrices per call, measured on the CPU with tracemalloc): 16.8 / 2.24 / 1.88 times the dense $M^2$ uint32 matrix at $n=4,5,6$, falling with $M$; at $n=7$ that is at most $1.88\cdot11.7\approx22$ GiB [extrapolation].

text: The first A100 run at $n=7$ (16.10.2026, main 53658b5) ran out of memory: rounds 0–3 in 3 / 26 / 57 / 85 s (rank 3 962 → 20 975 → 33 142 → 38 258), the pool peak 3.7 → 12.3 → 25.0 → 38.8 GiB, and round 4 failed to allocate 3.4 GB. The CPU measurement missed two things that only show at $n=7$: the shifts were fed whole from column 0, so all their rows entered the pool at the first panel at full width; and the trailing update went by tiles of 16 384 rows, i.e. 3.7 GB per temporary at $M=55\,986$, with four of them (the gathered rows, the product, the sum, the mask), plus three pool-sized copies when the pool was rebuilt. Now: a shift is a stream of pieces of 2 048 rows of $B$, each built when howell() reaches its leading column (the shifts map the columns monotonically, so the pieces come in increasing $c_0$; the streams are merged by $c_0$) — the shifted rows lead mostly in the top degree, so they join late and narrower; the tiles are of $2^{29}$ bytes, with two temporaries; the pool is rebuilt into one new buffer; the CuPy cache is returned to the driver when it holds more than 4 GiB unused; step 8 takes one shift per call (--group 1). The same results on the CPU ($n=4,5,6$, all hashes), the closure at $n=6$ in 203 s instead of 368 s, the peak 1.64 instead of 1.88 dense matrices.
